inside.title: What's inside
inside.lead: Everything below is in this repository right now, wired and working.
inside.authText: Email/password login, short-lived JWT access, rotating refresh cookie with reuse detection, role guards on every admin route.
inside.datatableText: Paginated, searchable, server-filtered user management over a typed API client. The password never leaves the API.
inside.uiText: 30+ Material Design 3 components: buttons, fields, overlays, a WYSIWYG editor, and honest empty, loading, error states.
inside.sharedText: One TypeScript package holds UserRole, API envelopes, and entity types, compiled to CJS/ESM and consumed by both apps.
inside.dockerText: Docker Compose brings up Postgres, Redis, object storage, and Mailpit. One env file at the root drives both apps.

why.title: Why a NestJS API — not fullstack Nuxt
why.lead: Nitro is a great app server. But when the API is a product — many clients, background work, strict contracts — a dedicated backend pays for itself.
why.c1x: One API serves the web app today — mobile apps, partners, and scripts tomorrow. Clients consume typed contracts, not server routes welded to a website.
why.c2x: Dependency injection, guards, pipes, interceptors, and OpenAPI/Swagger out of the box — the patterns production backends run on, not conventions you assemble yourself.
why.c3x: Queues, cron schedulers, and WebSockets are first-class in the Nest ecosystem — no long-running work parked inside the SSR process.
why.c4x: Deploy and scale the API and the web app separately — different images, different pace. The web can even go fully static while the API keeps evolving.
why.note: Still a Nuxt purist? The web app talks to any API — point apiBase elsewhere and keep the frontend.
